incentives.label: Federal clean electricity investment tax credit (Section 48E)
incentives.note: Not applied. IRS Notice 2025-42 (August 2025): under Public Law 119-21 (OBBBA) the Section 48E credit ends for solar facilities placed in service after December 31, 2027 unless construction began by July 4, 2026 (Physical Work Test). A new project would need to be in service by the end of 2027. Rate per the IRS Clean Electricity Investment Credit page (reviewed January 5, 2026): 6% base, up to 30% with prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements, plus 10 points each for domestic content and energy communities; foreign-entity rules also apply. Confirm eligibility with a tax adviser, then enter the amount.
incentives.source: IRS Notice 2025-42 (n-25-42.pdf); IRS Clean Electricity Investment Credit page (reviewed 05-Jan-2026).

incentives.label: ComEd standard incentive: LED fixtures and retrofits
incentives.note: Program rules (ComEd 2026 Standard Incentives Application (V15)): pre-approval is required for projects requesting $10,000 or more (otherwise ComEd may cap the incentive at $10,000); the incentive cannot exceed 90% of the incremental measure cost or 90% of the project cost, whichever is less (modeled as 90% of the upgrade's cost); funds are limited and subject to availability; final amounts depend on verified equipment. Rate: $0.75 per watt reduced. Watts reduced are estimated from the hotel's modeled lighting load (150 W per guest room and 1.0 W per ft2 of public areas and corridors, equipment.json placeholders) times the LED reduction, so the amount is an estimate. The rate is from the 2025 worksheet; confirm the 2026 lighting rate before applying.
incentives.source: ComEd Indoor Lighting Incentives Worksheet, January 1 - December 31, 2025 (updated November 5, 2025); ComEd 2026 Standard Incentives Application (V15)

incentives.label: ComEd standard incentive: lighting occupancy sensors
incentives.note: Program rules (ComEd 2026 Standard Incentives Application (V15)): pre-approval is required for projects requesting $10,000 or more (otherwise ComEd may cap the incentive at $10,000); the incentive cannot exceed 90% of the incremental measure cost or 90% of the project cost, whichever is less (modeled as 90% of the upgrade's cost); funds are limited and subject to availability; final amounts depend on verified equipment. Rate: $0.25 per watt controlled (new sensors only; replacing existing controls is not eligible). Watts controlled are the modeled public-area and corridor lighting load (1.0 W per ft2, placeholder) times the share covered.
incentives.source: ComEd Indoor Lighting Incentives Worksheet, January 1 - December 31, 2025 (updated November 5, 2025); ComEd 2026 Standard Incentives Application (V15)

incentives.label: ComEd standard incentive: guest room energy management (gas heat, electric AC)
incentives.note: Program rules (ComEd 2026 Standard Incentives Application (V15)): pre-approval is required for projects requesting $10,000 or more (otherwise ComEd may cap the incentive at $10,000); the incentive cannot exceed 90% of the incremental measure cost or 90% of the project cost, whichever is less (modeled as 90% of the upgrade's cost); funds are limited and subject to availability; final amounts depend on verified equipment. Rate: $75 per cooling ton controlled for guest rooms with natural gas heat and electric air conditioning; occupancy or key-card control with at least a 5 F unoccupied setback; new installations only. Tons are estimated at 0.75 ton per room (assumption). Your gas company may offer an additional rebate (not included).
incentives.source: ComEd HVAC and VSD Incentives Worksheet, January 1 - December 31, 2026 (updated May 4, 2026); ComEd 2026 Standard Incentives Application (V15)

incentives.label: ComEd standard incentive: guest room energy management (electric or heat-pump heat)
incentives.note: Program rules (ComEd 2026 Standard Incentives Application (V15)): pre-approval is required for projects requesting $10,000 or more (otherwise ComEd may cap the incentive at $10,000); the incentive cannot exceed 90% of the incremental measure cost or 90% of the project cost, whichever is less (modeled as 90% of the upgrade's cost); funds are limited and subject to availability; final amounts depend on verified equipment. Rate: $100 per cooling ton controlled for guest rooms with electric resistance or heat-pump heating and air conditioning. Tons are estimated at 0.75 ton per room (assumption).
incentives.source: ComEd HVAC and VSD Incentives Worksheet, January 1 - December 31, 2026 (updated May 4, 2026); ComEd 2026 Standard Incentives Application (V15)

incentives.label: ComEd standard incentives: high-efficiency HVAC equipment
incentives.note: Not applied: the 2026 rates depend on rated efficiency, which the model does not track. Water-cooled chillers $10 and air-cooled $7 per ton for each 0.01 kW/ton of IPLV below the qualifying efficiency; rooftop units $20 per ton per point of IEER/SEER2 above the requirement; PTAC/PTHP $30 per ton (under 2 tons). Enter an amount once the equipment is chosen.
incentives.source: ComEd HVAC and VSD Incentives Worksheet, January 1 - December 31, 2026 (updated May 4, 2026)

source: Programs that may lower the upfront cost. Modular: each program has an amount rule (kind and value) and is applied only when 'applied' and 'verified' are both true; until then it is shown as listed, with status 'unverified' and $0 in every calculation. No incentive amounts are invented. A user can enter a confirmed amount per upgrade, which replaces program amounts for that upgrade.
